question: The DE plan needs quantified expression, but this environment cannot quantify the 6 FASTQ samples: no aligner/quasi-mapper is installed (no Salmon, Kallisto, STAR, HISAT2, or featureCounts — the CLI track is empty and nothing installs at runtime), and there is no transcriptome sequence in the reference store (only the GRCh38.p13 genome FASTA and the GENCODE v50 GTF annotation, no pre-built quantification index). Please provide one of: (1) a gene-level raw count matrix (integer counts per gene × 6 samples, sample IDs matching metadata.csv), e.g. from STAR+featureCounts; (2) per-sample transcript quantifications (Salmon quant.sf or kallisto abundance.h5) plus a transcript-to-gene map; or (3) have the host provision a human reference transcriptome (Salmon index or transcript FASTA + GENCODE GTF) and a quantifier, and I will re-plan with an explicit quantification step. Once counts are available, I will run the treated-vs-control DE plan (QC, filtering, DESeq2 modeling, LFC shrinkage, FDR).

input.questionContext: Dataset: human liver bulk RNA-seq, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. Inputs: paired-end FASTQ (6 samples, /eval-four-models-v2-with-fastq-input-s1-1/data/inputs/reads) and metadata.csv with a condition column. The inputs are reads only — no count matrix or abundance table is present. The knowledge procedure (rule R-0020, flag outcome stop_quantify_first) states a differential-expression plan cannot start on FASTQ input: quantification (aligner/mapper choice, reference, decoys, annotation) must be resolved first, and the DE rules then apply to counts. Environment check: CLI package track is empty; Python/R inventories contain no salmon/kallisto/STAR/HISAT2/subread/featureCounts; reference store holds GENCODE v50 GTF (annotation only, no sequences), the PharmCAT GRCh38.p13 genome FASTA (pharmacogenomics bundle), UniProt ID mappings, pathway GMTs — no transcriptome FASTA and no quantification index.

flags.message: If the input is FASTQ reads, the differential expression plan cannot start. Quantification is an upstream step with its own decisions: the aligner or the mapper, the reference, the decoys, and the annotation. Each of these decisions changes the abundance estimates. Stop, and ask for a count matrix from an alignment pipeline or for the transcript quantifications from Salmon or kallisto. Then continue with the count rules.
